clusters.name: Morrison Cluster
clusters.description: A neutral cluster with occupied Future Settlers League (FSL) settlements, strategic SolPAC interests, and Iris Federation (IF) research outposts.
detail: Star systems: 4 known.
Part of a secondary FTL Lane that connects the Local and Homestead clusters.

clusters.name: Local Cluster
detail: Star systems: 5 known.

clusters.name: Homestead Cluster
clusters.description: All systems are under Iris Federation (IF) control, excluding the MACE-controlled Veranda system.
detail: Star systems: 2 known.

systems.name: Sol System
systems.description: Humanity's home system and the capital of SolPAC.

systems.name: Alpha Centuri
systems.description: The nearest star system to Sol, roughly 4.37 light-years away.
detail: Its yellow dwarf and orange dwarf orbit closely as a binary pair; Sol's actual nearest star, the red dwarf Proxima Centauri, is a much more distant companion not counted here.
Proxima Centauri hosts its own rocky planet, Proxima b, sitting within its habitable zone.

systems.name: Barnard's Star
systems.description: A red dwarf roughly 5.96 light-years from Sol, and one of the closest stars to it.
detail: Home to a candidate super-Earth, Barnard's Star b, discovered in 2018.

systems.name: Wolf
systems.description: Wolf 359, a faint red dwarf roughly 7.86 light-years from Sol.
detail: Despite decades of searching, no planets have been confirmed around it — its frequent, violent flares make detection unusually difficult.

systems.name: Lalande
systems.description: Lalande 21185, a red dwarf roughly 8.31 light-years from Sol.
detail: Its closest neighbor, Wolf 359, sits only about 4 light-years away — closer to it than to any other system in this cluster.
Home to a confirmed super-Earth, Lalande 21185 b, on a tight 13-day orbit.

systems.name: Huntington
systems.description: A binary star system home to the gas giants G-HX6T and G-SKHY, and the abandoned relay station Relay D2155.
detail: Its two stars, Alpha and Beta, are known locally by those names; Beta is a white dwarf, the dim remnant of a star that burned out long ago.

systems.name: Priapus
systems.description: Home to the planets Chaq and Lyon, the volcanic world Gibil, and three largely uncharted gas and ice giants.

systems.name: Ngozi
systems.description: Home to Gaia, a wetland world settled by the Future Settlers League, alongside the ocean world Nautilus and the gas/ice giants G-Z0XL and G-X4T6.

systems.name: Zuni
systems.description: A double star system home to the gas giant G-33UY and the planet Taishan.
detail: Its two stars are known locally as Zuni Major, a yellow dwarf, and Zuni Minor, a smaller orange dwarf.

systems.name: Iris
systems.description: Named in the cluster's notes; no further orbital detail has been recorded yet.

systems.name: Veranda
systems.description: Named in the cluster's notes; no further orbital detail has been recorded yet.

systems.name: Thalla
systems.description: Named in the cluster's notes; no further orbital detail has been recorded yet.

systems.name: Talvern
systems.description: A yellow dwarf system with no known life, marked only by a scattered asteroid belt.

systems.name: Ustrid
systems.description: An orange dwarf system with no known life, marked only by two ice giants and a scattered asteroid belt.

systems.name: Grivane
systems.description: An orange dwarf system with no known life, marked only by a scattered asteroid belt.

systems.name: Lundstrom
systems.description: A red dwarf system with no known life, marked only by two barren worlds and a gas giant.

systems.name: Corrigan
systems.description: An orange dwarf system with no known life, marked only by a gas giant.

systems.name: Casimund
systems.description: An orange dwarf system with no known life, marked only by two barren worlds and an ice giant.

systems.name: Harrowick
systems.description: A yellow dwarf system with no known life, marked only by a barren world.

systems.name: Bramsk
systems.description: A red dwarf system with no known life, marked only by a barren world.

systems.name: Nabren
systems.description: A red dwarf system with no known life, marked only by an ice giant and a scattered asteroid belt.

orbitalBodies.name: Pertash Belt
orbitalBodies.description: A scattered belt of rocky debris.

orbitalBodies.name: Halcost
orbitalBodies.description: An ice giant with roughly 29 moons, none yet catalogued.

orbitalBodies.name: Mirsk
orbitalBodies.description: An ice giant with roughly 71 moons, none yet catalogued.

orbitalBodies.name: Thornix Belt
orbitalBodies.description: A scattered belt of rocky debris.

orbitalBodies.name: Ferrin Belt
orbitalBodies.description: A scattered belt of rocky debris.

orbitalBodies.name: Kelmyr
orbitalBodies.description: A frozen rocky world locked in permanent ice.

orbitalBodies.name: Feldis
orbitalBodies.description: A gas giant with roughly 159 moons, none yet catalogued.

orbitalBodies.name: Odessyn
orbitalBodies.description: A scorched rocky world, far too hot to support life.

orbitalBodies.name: Jastrun
orbitalBodies.description: A gas giant with roughly 142 moons, none yet catalogued.

orbitalBodies.name: Ingvar
orbitalBodies.description: A barren rocky world with no atmosphere.

orbitalBodies.name: Junnar
orbitalBodies.description: A barren rocky world with no atmosphere.

orbitalBodies.name: Driscol
orbitalBodies.description: An ice giant with roughly 57 moons, none yet catalogued.

orbitalBodies.name: Kavrel
orbitalBodies.description: A scorched rocky world, far too hot to support life.

orbitalBodies.name: Verrow
orbitalBodies.description: A frozen rocky world locked in permanent ice.

orbitalBodies.name: Baltrun
orbitalBodies.description: An ice giant with roughly 100 moons, none yet catalogued.

orbitalBodies.name: Solmere Belt
orbitalBodies.description: A scattered belt of rocky debris.

orbitalBodies.name: Proxima b
orbitalBodies.description: A rocky planet orbiting Proxima Centauri, the binary pair's much more distant third companion; sits within its habitable zone, though true surface conditions remain unknown.
detail: Roughly 1.07 times Earth's mass, discovered via radial velocity in 2016.
Proxima Centauri's frequent, powerful flares may strip away any atmosphere it has.

orbitalBodies.name: Barnard's Star b
orbitalBodies.description: A super-Earth candidate orbiting just outside Barnard's Star's habitable zone — likely too cold to hold liquid water on its surface.
detail: Roughly 3.2 times Earth's mass, detected via radial velocity in 2018.
Orbits its dim red dwarf star once every 233 days.

orbitalBodies.name: Lalande 21185 b
orbitalBodies.description: A super-Earth on a tight, roughly 13-day orbit around Lalande 21185, confirmed after decades of disputed detections.
detail: Roughly 3 times Earth's mass, confirmed in 2021 from combined radial-velocity data.
Orbits far too close to its star for any reasonable chance of habitability.

orbitalBodies.name: Mercury
orbitalBodies.description: The smallest planet in the solar system, and the closest to the Sun.
detail: Daytime temperatures top 400°C, but with no atmosphere to hold heat, nights plunge to nearly -180°C.

orbitalBodies.name: Venus
orbitalBodies.description: The hottest planet in the solar system, hotter even than Mercury.
detail: A runaway greenhouse effect traps heat under thick clouds of sulfuric acid, driving surface temperatures above 460°C.

orbitalBodies.name: Earth
orbitalBodies.description: Humanity's homeworld, one of countless life-bearing worlds across the galaxy.
detail: Liquid water covers roughly 70% of its surface.

orbitalBodies.name: ISS Initiative
orbitalBodies.description: The largest known space station, and the largest transfer station in the Local Cluster.
detail: Before Hrava accelerator technology was adopted, it served as humanity's only means of FTL travel; now it's a sprawling spaceport city.
Home to roughly 15,000 permanent residents, though it relies entirely on imported resources.
Its rental spaces, transfer capacity, and enterprise market provide most of the financial support that keeps the station running.

orbitalBodies.name: Mars
orbitalBodies.description: A cold desert world, home to the largest volcano and canyon system in the solar system.
detail: Olympus Mons stands nearly three times the height of Mount Everest.
Valles Marineris stretches roughly the width of the continental United States.

orbitalBodies.name: Asteroid Belt
orbitalBodies.description: A ring of rocky debris between Mars and Jupiter.
detail: Likely material that never coalesced into a planet, kept stirred up by Jupiter's gravity.

orbitalBodies.name: Jupiter
orbitalBodies.description: The largest planet in the solar system.
detail: Its Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth that has raged for centuries.
Has no solid surface to land on.
Beyond its four largest (Galilean) moons, around 90 more, much smaller moons are known.

orbitalBodies.name: Saturn
orbitalBodies.description: Famous for its wide, prominent ring system.
detail: The rings are made almost entirely of ice particles, ranging from dust-sized grains to boulders.
Has no solid surface to land on.
Beyond Titan and Enceladus, well over 100 more, much smaller moons are known.

orbitalBodies.name: Uranus
orbitalBodies.description: An ice giant that rotates almost completely on its side.
detail: Its axis is tilted roughly 98 degrees, likely the result of an ancient collision — its ring system, aligned with its equator, is tilted right along with it, standing almost on end compared to Saturn's rings.
Has a faint ring system of its own: narrower and much darker than Saturn's, discovered in 1977 and not directly photographed until decades later.
Has no solid surface to land on.
Beyond its five major moons, around 20 more, much smaller moons are known.

orbitalBodies.name: Neptune
orbitalBodies.description: The most distant planet from the Sun, and the windiest.
detail: Wind speeds can exceed 2,000 km/h, the fastest recorded in the solar system.
Has no solid surface to land on.
Beyond Triton, around 15 more, much smaller moons are known.

orbitalBodies.name: Pluto
orbitalBodies.description: A distant dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt.
detail: Reclassified from a full planet in 2006, but still commonly counted among the Sun's family of worlds.
Average surface temperature hovers around -240°C, among the coldest in the solar system.
Beyond Charon, four much smaller moons are known: Styx, Nix, Kerberos, and Hydra.

orbitalBodies.name: Lyon
orbitalBodies.description: A cold planet, home to the CC Primary Relay MC-134 station.

orbitalBodies.name: Gibil
orbitalBodies.description: A volcanic world with a toxic atmosphere.

orbitalBodies.name: G-21T5
orbitalBodies.description: A gas giant with roughly 25 moons, including the volcanic Small Drake and Big Drake.

orbitalBodies.name: Chaq
orbitalBodies.description: Home to Chaq Madee, a desert island settlement where the sun never sets.

orbitalBodies.name: G-8ZSW
orbitalBodies.description: An ice giant with roughly 50 moons, including the ocean moon Cove and the icy moon Rime.

orbitalBodies.name: G-9QRJ
orbitalBodies.description: An ice giant with roughly 25 moons, none yet catalogued in detail.

orbitalBodies.name: Nautilus
orbitalBodies.description: A world of sand and water, with a breathable atmosphere.

orbitalBodies.name: Gaia
orbitalBodies.description: A world of sprawling wetlands, settled by the Future Settlers League.

orbitalBodies.name: G-Z0XL
orbitalBodies.description: A gas giant with roughly 150 moons and a tight ring of dust, five of which are named.

orbitalBodies.name: G-X4T6
orbitalBodies.description: An ice giant with roughly 50 moons, including the jungle moon Balboa.

orbitalBodies.name: Taishan
orbitalBodies.description: Home to Pearl Valley, the largest city in the Morrison Cluster; no further detail has been recorded yet.

orbitalBodies.name: G-33UY
orbitalBodies.description: A gas giant with layered rings of ice and three known moons.

orbitalBodies.name: G-HX6T
orbitalBodies.description: A gas giant with roughly 150 moons and a partial ring of dust, including the rocky moon Flint.

orbitalBodies.name: G-SKHY
orbitalBodies.description: A gas giant with roughly 50 moons, including the icy moon Fannif.

orbitalBodies.name: Relay D2155
orbitalBodies.description: An abandoned Galac-Tech station originally used to develop the MOC-L.
detail: Once hosted communication relays and cargo transfers.
Its communication relays are still active, handling a small portion of the Morrison Cluster's overflow traffic.

moons.name: Orca
moons.description: A medium moon covered in toxic oceans.

moons.name: Shellus
moons.description: A small, sandy moon with no atmosphere.

moons.name: Sirrah
moons.description: Named in Gaia's notes; no further detail has been recorded yet.

moons.name: Ada
moons.description: Named in Gaia's notes; no further detail has been recorded yet.

moons.name: Balboa
moons.description: A small moon with a thick atmosphere and dense jungle cover, unusual for an ice giant's moon.

moons.name: Kelver
moons.description: A medium jungle moon with a toxic atmosphere.

moons.name: Thrum
moons.description: A medium jungle moon with a toxic atmosphere.

moons.name: Yarrow
moons.description: A small jungle moon with a toxic atmosphere.

moons.name: Cindra
moons.description: A small volcanic moon with a thin atmosphere.

moons.name: Molt
moons.description: A small rocky moon with a thin atmosphere.

moons.name: Cove
moons.description: A small ocean moon with a thin atmosphere.

moons.name: Rime
moons.description: A small moon of ice and rock, with no atmosphere.

moons.name: Flint
moons.description: A small rocky moon with no atmosphere.

moons.name: Pike
moons.description: A small, rocky moon with a thin atmosphere.

moons.name: Small Drake
moons.description: A small volcanic moon with no atmosphere.

moons.name: Big Drake
moons.description: A medium volcanic moon with no atmosphere, larger than its neighbor Small Drake.

moons.name: Taizou
moons.description: A medium rocky moon with a thin atmosphere.

moons.name: Guy 4
moons.description: An icy rock with pure H2O deposits.

moons.name: Karst
moons.description: A small desert moon with a breathable atmosphere.

moons.name: Scree
moons.description: A small rocky moon with no atmosphere.

moons.name: Fannif
moons.description: A medium moon of mixed ice and rock, with a thin atmosphere.

moons.name: Moon
moons.description: Earth's only natural satellite.

moons.name: Phobos
moons.description: The larger and closer of Mars's two moons.
detail: Slowly spiraling inward; expected to eventually break apart or crash into Mars.

moons.name: Deimos
moons.description: The smaller and more distant of Mars's two moons.

moons.name: Io
moons.description: The most volcanically active body in the solar system.

moons.name: Europa
moons.description: An icy moon believed to hide a liquid water ocean beneath its surface.

moons.name: Ganymede
moons.description: The largest moon in the solar system, bigger than the planet Mercury.

moons.name: Callisto
moons.description: One of the most heavily cratered bodies in the solar system.

moons.name: Titan
moons.description: Saturn's largest moon, and the only moon in the solar system with a dense atmosphere.
detail: Has liquid lakes and seas on its surface, though of methane and ethane rather than water.

moons.name: Enceladus
moons.description: An icy moon with geysers venting water vapor from a subsurface ocean near its south pole.

moons.name: Miranda
moons.description: The smallest and innermost of Uranus's five major moons, with a dramatically varied, patchwork surface.

moons.name: Ariel
moons.description: The brightest of Uranus's major moons.

moons.name: Umbriel
moons.description: The darkest of Uranus's major moons.

moons.name: Titania
moons.description: The largest moon of Uranus.

moons.name: Oberon
moons.description: The outermost of Uranus's five major moons.

moons.name: Triton
moons.description: Neptune's largest moon, orbiting backwards relative to Neptune's rotation.
detail: Likely a captured Kuiper Belt object rather than a moon formed alongside Neptune.

moons.name: Charon
moons.description: Pluto's largest moon, so large relative to Pluto that the two orbit a point in space between them.

locations.name: Chaq Madee
locations.description: A large desert island formed at the "eye" of Chaq, where the sun never sets.
detail: Its semi-tropical coast is lined with settlements and surrounded by a large salty ocean; its climate and composition are much like Earth's.
Settled by the Future Settlers League.

locations.name: Permafreeze
locations.description: The sunless side of Chaq, covered in floating permafrost.

locations.name: CC Primary Relay MC-134
locations.description: A large relay station on Lyon's northern ice cap that handles much of the Morrison Cluster's inter-cluster network communication.
detail: Operated by Capital Communications.

locations.name: Re-sourced Recycling HQ
locations.description: An orbital transfer station that collects material from Small Drake and shuttles it to recycling and waste-processing plants on the surface.

locations.name: RS Vineless
locations.description: An abandoned Altoa Research facility that studied invasive plant life carried across G-Z0XL's moons.

locations.name: Brady Station
locations.description: An active mining station in orbit around G-HX6T.

locations.name: Fountain
locations.description: A small dome settlement that uses heated domes and tunnels to protect it from Guy 4's frozen landscape.
detail: Collects and refines pure H2O for export, shipping water, hydrogen fuel, and oxygen through the Drop and Go Network.
Home to an independent system com relay.

locations.name: Old Melt
locations.description: The first mine on Guy 4, and the economic lifeline for Fountain during its founding years.
detail: Retired after twenty years of service, following a series of minor cave-ins that raised structural concerns.
Equipment can still be found in its tunnels, particularly ones cut off entirely by collapses.

locations.name: Snowed Inn
locations.description: A standard inn in Fountain catering to the settlement's few travelers.
detail: Owned and operated by Larry for at least ten years.
Offers standard room stays with optional meals, off-moon travel arrangements, and public network terminals.

locations.name: Whitefish Harbor
locations.description: Named in Gaia's notes; no further detail has been recorded yet.

locations.name: Peaty Planes
locations.description: Named in Gaia's notes; no further detail has been recorded yet.

locations.name: Dredge River
locations.description: Named in Gaia's notes; no further detail has been recorded yet.

locations.name: Outlaw Compound
locations.description: A former research warehouse turned into a small compound.
detail: Its structures and landing space have been kept in very good condition despite their surroundings.

locations.name: Pearl Valley
locations.description: The largest city in the Morrison Cluster, built in the valley where Taishan's first settlement began.
detail: Feng Chenyue is credited with its official founding, and served as its first mayor. A large statue of her likeness is located in Founder's Plaza, a conversion of the original spaceport.
Pearl Valley's spaceport has a small orbital station linked with it that organizes out of system traffic.
